info.bio: Si bien nacieron en Inglaterra durante la explosión punk de 1977, los Psychedelic Furs delinearon un estilo que encuentra sus influencias primarias tanto en el sonido agresivo de los Sex Pistols como en el glam de David Bowie o Roxy Music y pinceladas de rock psicodélico. Con la idea firme de escapar a cualquier tipo de rótulo, los hermanos Richard (vocalista) y Tim Butler (bajista) sentaron las bases de una banda a la que enseguida se sumaron el saxofonista Duncan Kilburn y el guitarrista Roger Morris.

scenes.name: Dark punk y rock gótico
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El punk británico estuvo flanqueado desde el principio por un movimiento «gótico» que canalizaba su violencia hacia atmósferas de terror y rituales esotéricos: Stranglers, Siouxsie, X-Ray Spex. Lo más interesante evita el tono de película de terror: The Cure introducen la angustia existencial de Camus y Sartre (Pornography, Disintegration); Joy Division mezclan Doors, Kraftwerk y Black Sabbath y su final anuncia el synth-pop; Bauhaus, Killing Joke, Psychedelic Furs, los irlandeses Virgin Prunes y la cima del género, Public Image Ltd de Johnny Lydon, que convierte el punk en música de cámara con dub y ecos étnicos (Second Edition, Flowers Of Romance). Después, el gótico bailable de Sisters Of Mercy, Alien Sex Fiend, Cult, Mission e In The Nursery.

podcast.title: John Hughes Film Exposure (1980s)
podcast.body: The Psychedelic Furs were among the bands whose music was heavily mined for the soundtracks of John Hughes' 1980s films. These carefully curated soundtracks played a significant role in exposing numerous North American audiences to various alternative rock acts, particularly British performers. "So many people learned of bands like The Specials and Spandovalet and Billy Idle and General Public and Wang Chung and Yellow and New Order and the Psychedelic Furs and the Smiths and Echo and the Bunyman, Susanne Vagan in excess the Jesus and Mary chain, Flesh for Luluo and so many others from those soundtrack albums."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Produced by Steve Lillywhite
podcast.body: Steve Lillywhite, who produced records for The Psychedelic Furs, sold his royalties from his work. "Steve Lillewight, who produced records for everyone from Susie in the Banshees and the psychedelic furs to the killers in Peter Gabriel and you too, sold his royalties."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unrealized Album Project
podcast.body: David Botrell and Bob Lannwaw were slated to work on the next Psychedelic Furs record. However, the project did not proceed because the band had no songs written for rehearsal, and Lannwaw, having just spent a year and a half with an artist who wrote as they went, declined to continue. "Dan was slated to do the next psychedelic furs record and I went down with him to rehearse at John Giblin's rehearsal studio in Surrey"

xref.title: First Recordings (1986)
xref.body: The earliest existing recording attributed to the band is a five-track cassette from 1986, which they self-issued at Abingdon. At this point, Johnny Greenwood was not yet a member, but a sax player named Razz Peterson was part of the lineup. The tape prominently featured 80s influences from bands like U2, Waterboys, Psychedelic Furs, and The Smiths, with Tom York handling lead vocals at 17 years old. "The earliest recording that seems to exist is a 1986 cassette that was recorded at Elbington."

xref.title: Influenced Major Artists
xref.body: The Velvet Underground is credited with awakening and influencing a wide array of prominent artists and bands, including David Bowie, Roxy Music, The Doors, Patti Smith, Iggy Pop and the Stooges, U2, Joy Division, The Pixies, The Sex Pistols, Talking Heads, The Cure, Kraftwerk, R.E.M., Simple Minds, The Strokes, and The Psychedelic Furs, whose name derived from a Velvet Underground song. "Here is a list of just some of the few who claimed to have been awakened by the velvet underground and then incorporated some of whatever they were doing into their music."

xref.title: John Hughes Film Exposure (1980s)
xref.body: The Specials were one of many bands whose music was heavily mined for the soundtracks of John Hughes' 1980s films. These carefully curated soundtracks played a significant role in introducing a wide audience in North America to bands from the alternative rock scene, particularly British performers. "So many people learned of bands like The Specials and Spandovalet and Billy Idle and General Public and Wang Chung and Yellow and New Order and the Psychedelic Furs and the Smiths and Echo and the Bunyman, Susanne Vagan in excess the Jesus and Mary chain, Flesh for Luluo and so many others from those soundtrack albums."
